annotations.description: Only 2 of 3 brokers are reachable; the cluster tolerates one loss.

diagnosis.summary: Broker lakehouse-dual-role-0 is Running/Ready in Kubernetes but its Prometheus metrics scrape is failing, causing the alert to count only 2/3 brokers as reachable. All brokers suffered a simultaneous chaos-mesh-induced kill ~129 minutes ago; the other two brokers fully recovered, but broker-0 still shows 60 under-replicated partitions and active_controllers=0 (no KRaft controller visible from scraped metrics). No partitions are offline or below min-ISR, so writes still succeed, but the cluster has zero fault-tolerance margin until broker-0 is healthy.
diagnosis.root_cause: A chaos-mesh experiment (chaos-mesh-local deployed 133 minutes ago) killed all Kafka broker pods simultaneously with exit_code 255/Unknown. Brokers 1 and 2 recovered fully. Broker-0 (lakehouse-dual-role-0, zone-b/lakehouse-worker2) restarted and passes Kubernetes liveness/readiness probes but its JMX/metrics endpoint is not being scraped by Prometheus (brokers_scraped_up=false for broker-0 only). This makes Prometheus see only 2/3 brokers reachable and fires KafkaBrokerDown. The 60 under-replicated partitions and active_controllers=0 (which is derived only from scraped brokers—broker-0 may be the KRaft controller) indicate broker-0 is in a degraded state despite passing K8s health checks.
diagnosis.impact: No data loss and no write stoppage yet (0 offline partitions, 0 below-min-ISR partitions). However, the cluster is operating with zero fault-tolerance: loss of any second broker would stop all writes. Flink consumer lag is 200 messages (minor). The cluster will remain at risk until broker-0 fully rejoins and all 60 under-replicated partitions are caught up.

evidence.finding: All 3 broker pods phase=Running ready=1/1, but brokers_scraped_up shows lakehouse-dual-role-0=false. under_replicated_partitions=60, under_min_isr_partitions=0, offline_partitions=0, active_controllers=0. All brokers last terminated ~129 minutes ago with exit_code 255/Unknown. Consumer lag flink-events-to-iceberg=200.

All kafka namespace pods Running/Ready. lakehouse-dual-role-0, kafka-admin, lakehouse-kafka-exporter all on lakehouse-worker2 all terminated 129.3 min ago (exit_code 255/Unknown). strimzi-cluster-operator terminated 117.1 min ago (exit_code 1/Error). Brokers on worker and worker3 also terminated ~129 min ago.
All 3 worker nodes Ready, no pressure conditions, no cordons. Workers span zone-a, zone-b, zone-c — no node failure.

chaos-mesh-local was deployed 133 minutes ago (revision 9187ff9e9e6f), approximately 4 minutes before the mass pod-kill event at ~129 minutes ago — consistent with a chaos experiment triggering the disruption.
Flink job RUNNING/STABLE, started 127.9 min ago (recovered from checkpoint after the chaos event). 28 completed checkpoints in last 5 min, 0 failed. Consumer lag 200.
Runbook docs/runbooks/kafka.md#kafkabrokerdown: Strimzi restarts crashed brokers automatically; check pod/node state and logs. Do not delete PVC.

proposed_action.rationale: Broker-0 is in a wedged state: its Kubernetes health probes pass but Prometheus cannot scrape its metrics endpoint, there are 60 under-replicated partitions attributed to it, and active_controllers=0 (broker-0 is likely the KRaft controller whose metrics are dark). A pod restart via the StatefulSet is safe — Strimzi will recreate it with its existing PVC intact, the broker will rejoin the cluster, re-replicate the 60 partitions, and restore the metrics endpoint. The other two brokers are healthy and min-ISR=2 is still satisfied so there is no write interruption during the restart.

follow_ups: Review the chaos-mesh-local experiment deployed ~133 minutes ago (revision 9187ff9e9e6f) — confirm it was intentional and check if it has completed or should be torn down.
After broker-0 restarts, verify active_controllers returns to 1 and under_replicated_partitions drains to 0.
Investigate why strimzi-cluster-operator itself crashed with exit_code 1 (Error) ~117 minutes ago; ensure it is fully healthy.
Consider whether the chaos-mesh experiment schedule should be suspended in this environment to avoid unplanned disruptions during business hours.
Monitor Flink consumer lag (currently 200) to confirm it drains once broker-0 is fully in-sync.
